officialTitle: Concurrent once-daily versus twice-daily chemoradiotherapy in patients with limited-stage small-cell lung cancer (CONVERT): an open-label, phase 3, randomised, superiority trial

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Between April 7, 2008, and Nov 29, 2013, 547 patients were enrolled and randomly assigned to receive twice-daily concurrent chemoradiotherapy (274 patients) or once-daily concurrent chemoradiotherapy (273 patients).
design.notes: Designed to show superiority of once-daily 66 Gy over twice-daily 45 Gy; not powered for equivalence. Radiotherapy started on day 22 after commencing cisplatin-etoposide.

sponsor: Cancer Research UK and cooperative groups (academic)
clinicalQuestion: In limited-stage SCLC, is high-dose once-daily concurrent chemoradiotherapy superior to standard twice-daily accelerated chemoradiotherapy?

pico.population: Adults with limited-stage SCLC, ECOG PS 0-2, adequate pulmonary function
pico.intervention: Once-daily thoracic radiotherapy (66 Gy in 33 fractions) concurrent with cisplatin-etoposide
pico.comparator: Twice-daily thoracic radiotherapy (45 Gy in 30 fractions) concurrent with cisplatin-etoposide

arms.label: Twice-daily RT
arms.regimen: Cisplatin-etoposide with concurrent twice-daily thoracic radiotherapy
arms.dosing: 45 Gy in 30 twice-daily fractions of 1.5 Gy over 19 days
arms.doseSourceQuote: Patients were randomly assigned to receive either 45 Gy radiotherapy in 30 twice-daily fractions of 1·5 Gy over 19 days, or 66 Gy in 33 once-daily fractions of 2 Gy over 45 days, starting on day 22 after commencing cisplatin-etoposide chemotherapy (given as four to six cycles every 3 weeks in both groups).

arms.label: Once-daily RT
arms.regimen: Cisplatin-etoposide with concurrent once-daily thoracic radiotherapy
arms.dosing: 66 Gy in 33 once-daily fractions of 2 Gy over 45 days
arms.doseSourceQuote: Patients were randomly assigned to receive either 45 Gy radiotherapy in 30 twice-daily fractions of 1·5 Gy over 19 days, or 66 Gy in 33 once-daily fractions of 2 Gy over 45 days, starting on day 22 after commencing cisplatin-etoposide chemotherapy (given as four to six cycles every 3 weeks in both groups).

publications.title: Concurrent once-daily versus twice-daily chemoradiotherapy in patients with limited-stage small-cell lung cancer (CONVERT): an open-label, phase 3, randomised, superiority trial.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: At a median follow-up of 45 months (IQR 35-58), median overall survival was 30 months (95% CI 24-34) in the twice-daily group versus 25 months (21-31) in the once-daily group (hazard ratio for death in the once daily group 1·18 [95% CI 0·95-1·45]; p=0·14).
2-year overall survival was 56% (95% CI 50-62) in the twice-daily group and 51% (45-57) in the once-daily group (absolute difference between the treatment groups 5·3% [95% CI -3·2% to 13·7%]).

safety.sourceQuote: there was significantly more grade 4 neutropenia with twice-daily radiotherapy (129 [49%] vs 101 [38%]; p=0·05)

In patients assessed for radiotherapy toxicity, was no difference in grade 3-4 oesophagitis between the groups (47 [19%] of 254 patients in the twice-daily group vs 47 [19%] of 246 in the once-daily group; p=0·85)
11 patients died from treatment-related causes (three in the twice-daily group and eight in the once-daily group).

strengths: Large international randomised phase III trial with modern conformal radiotherapy
Mandatory radiotherapy quality assurance in a multinational setting
limitations: Designed for superiority of once-daily treatment; not powered to show equivalence
Radiotherapy started with the second chemotherapy cycle rather than the first

clinicalImplications.text: Once-daily high-dose radiotherapy did not outperform twice-daily treatment; the authors concluded twice-daily radiotherapy should remain the standard, while toxicity was similar and lower than expected in both arms.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Twice-daily remains the reference schedule; when logistics preclude it, once-daily high-dose regimens are a commonly used alternative with comparable observed outcomes but without formal proof of equivalence.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 28642008.
